inspiration: Sprite sheets as atlases: each building family lives on a large sheet cut into a fixed grid, and a selector maps building type to cell (buildingSprite.ts lines 62-74). Recreate: one atlas per family with a type-to-cell table, so new buildings need no code change.

State variants share one grid: construction, abandoned, park and dense versions sit on sheets with the same layout as the main sheet (skills/adding-asset-sheets.md line 28), so swapping a state is a sheet change, not a layout change. Recreate the same rule for our own states.

Priority list for which sheet to show: construction first, then abandoned, parks, dense or modern, farm, shops, stations, services, default (buildingSprite.ts lines 64-74). Recreate as an explicit ordered rule, documented in one place.

Key-colour cut-out: art is drawn on solid pure red and the loader drops pixels within a colour distance of that red (imageLoader.ts lines 7-8). It works, but true alpha PNG or WebP is cleaner. Recreate with alpha and keep the key only as a fallback.

Era and theme re-skins: one city family repainted for five eras (ages/) and one ride family repainted in two themes (coaster/theme_classic, theme_modern). Recreate with our own eras and palette families, not the same five.
Seaplane on a planes sheet row, with wakes on water and contrails in the air (drawAircraft.ts line 948). Recreate as a flying-boat row with two state frames.
Effect puffs and particles as typed effect lists: factory smog, clouds and fireworks (effectsSystems.ts line 2). Recreate as small typed particle sets with our own colours.

Asset sheet recipe for artists: 6 rows by 5 columns, solid red background, sprites centred in each cell so nothing is cut off (SKILL.md lines 14-15 and line 124). A human artist can use the same grid with originals.
